citation_audit.claim: Genie extends this idea toward interactive video worlds: the paper describes unsupervised training from unlabelled video, spatiotemporal tokenization, autoregressive dynamics, and frame-by-frame interaction via a latent action model [4].
citation_audit.evidence: The abstract says Genie is "the first generative interactive environment trained in an unsupervised manner from unlabelled Internet videos." It also states the model is "comprised of a spatiotemporal video tokenizer, an autoregressive dynamics model, and a simple and scalable latent action model," and that "Genie enables users to act in the generated environments on a frame-by-frame basis."

citation_audit.claim: WorldPrediction uses discriminative multiple-choice tests to distinguish the correct action or action sequence from counterfactual distractors, and separates single-step world-model judgment from long-horizon procedural planning [8].
citation_audit.evidence: The abstract says: "Given initial and final world states, the task is to distinguish the proper action (WorldPrediction-WM) or the properly ordered sequence of actions (WorldPrediction-PP) from a set of counterfactual distractors." It also says WorldPrediction is "a video-based benchmark for evaluating world modeling and procedural planning" and introduces two sub-benchmarks, WorldPrediction-WM and WorldPrediction-PP.
